questions.text: This city is an Eastern Kentucky economic center. What city holds an annual Hillbilly Days festival, and has its mascot Pikey the Bear?
This politician lends his name to a large lake in western Kentucky. What Kentuckian served as vice-president for Harry S. Truman?
What central Florida city is close to the Kennedy Space Center and home to over a dozen theme parks, including Legoland, Epcot, and Walt Disney World?
During this process, liquid rock cools. Then it hardens to form solid rock. Identify this complex process in the rock cycle?
This term refers to areas with relatively few people, and lots of forests and natural scenery. What is this five-letter term?

This trading company was granted a monopoly by its government to conduct trade, raise armies, and make treaties between the Cape of Good Hope at the southern tip of Africa and the Straits of Magellan between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. What was this giant trading company based in the Netherlands during the 1600s?
This planet is the only planet with just one moon. Its day is 24 hours and its year is 365.25 days. What terrestrial planet is the only planet in the solar system known to support human life?

Much of 1993 movie Hocus Pocus was filmed in this town. What Massachusetts city was the site of of the 1692 series of trials in which many, particularly young women, were accused of practicing witchcraft?

This invention was important in the American West, because it allowed ranchers to keep livestock from straying off their property. Today it can even be electrified. What invention typically consists of strands of flexible cable twisted around each other with spikes?

This man began his campaign for U.S. Senate with his "House Divided" speech. His final public address spurred John Wilkes Booth to assassinate him days later. Which president delivered the "Gettysburg Address"?

This global conflict was also known as The Great War. It featured fighting between two coalitions: the Allies, which included America, France and the United Kingdom, against the Central powers, which included Germany and Austria-Hungary. What global conflict featured trench warfare and poison gas, and began in 1914 and ended in 1918?
This number has been as low as six; it is not set by the constitution, but by congress. How many justices sit on the Supreme Court?

People convicted of this crime in America include abolitionist John Brown and the wartime Japan propagandist known as Tokyo Rose. What term describes the act of trying to overthrow the government or help its enemies?
During the Great Depression, this governmental labor statistic peaked at nearly 25%. What rate tells us what percent of people in the labor force do not have jobs?

This kind of folk art has a name coming from a British dialect meaning time waster. Whalers often practiced it while on their years-long voyage. Identify this practice of engraving designs on whalebone and walrus tusks.
This four-word slogan appears in the fourth verse of "The Star-Spangled Banner," on buildings, and on currency. In 1956, what was approved as our national motto?
This African-American surgeon was born in Washington, D.C. He organized the first blood bank in the United States. Who developed methods of storing blood plasma?
This Kentucky Politician had long struggled with polio. He began serving in the Senate in 1985. Who announced he would retire from leadership in politics in late 2024?
